skill.name: anndata
skill.description: Guidance for working with AnnData objects, H5AD and Zarr files, single-cell genomics datasets, metadata alignment, concatenation, and memory-efficient scverse workflows.
skill.summary: Guides AnnData object creation, I/O, manipulation, concatenation, and single-cell workflow patterns.

content.value_statement: AnnData workflows can fail from misaligned metadata, large files, and unclear storage choices. This skill gives focused guidance for object structure, I/O, concatenation, and memory-aware analysis.
actual_capabilities: Explains AnnData components such as X, obs, var, layers, obsm, varm, obsp, varp, uns, and raw.
Guides reading and writing H5AD, Zarr, CSV, MTX, Loom, 10X, and related data formats.
Provides patterns for concatenating batches, modalities, layers, and multidimensional annotations.
Recommends memory practices including sparse matrices, backed mode, chunked processing, and categorical metadata.
Helps diagnose metadata alignment, view-versus-copy behavior, index conflicts, and common AnnData pitfalls.
Connects AnnData workflows with Scanpy, Muon, PyTorch loaders, pandas, and scverse tooling.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not validate biological conclusions.
It does not execute analysis unless the host assistant or user runs the suggested Python commands.
Remote data examples use placeholders and require user-approved URLs, permissions, and data handling checks.
It does not replace package documentation for version-specific AnnData API changes.

use_cases.title: Prepare Single-Cell Data
use_cases.description: Create AnnData objects, load 10X or H5AD files, add metadata, and preserve raw counts before filtering.

use_cases.title: Scale Large Dataset Workflows
use_cases.description: Choose backed mode, sparse matrices, Zarr storage, chunking, and compression for memory-limited analysis.

use_cases.title: Standardize Multi-Batch Integration
use_cases.description: Concatenate datasets with batch labels, resolve index conflicts, and document merge choices for reproducibility.

prompt_templates.title: Understand AnnData Basics
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain the main parts of an AnnData object for a new single-cell RNA-seq project. Include what belongs in X, obs, var, layers, obsm, and uns.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Storage Format
prompt_templates.prompt: I have a large annotated matrix that may exceed memory. Recommend an AnnData storage format and access pattern, including H5AD, Zarr, backed mode, and compression tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Fix Metadata Alignment
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my AnnData metadata update plan. Explain how to avoid observation index misalignment, duplicate names, and view-versus-copy mistakes before I add external annotations.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Integration Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a reproducible workflow to concatenate multiple AnnData batches, preserve batch labels, choose join and merge strategies, optimize memory, and validate the combined object.

output_examples.input: A user asks which format to use for a 100 GB AnnData dataset stored in cloud storage.
output_examples.output: The response compares H5AD and Zarr, recommends lazy access, explains chunk size tradeoffs, and lists validation checks before writing results.

output_examples.input: A user asks why added sample metadata no longer matches cells after filtering.
output_examples.output: The response identifies index alignment as the likely issue and recommends joining by observation names with uniqueness checks.

output_examples.input: A user asks how to merge three sequencing batches while keeping source labels.
output_examples.output: The response outlines a concatenation plan using batch labels, consistent variable names, merge strategy selection, and post-merge sanity checks.

best_practices: Store raw counts before filtering or normalization so later analysis can reference the original measurements.
Use sparse matrices, categorical metadata, and backed mode when datasets are large or memory constrained.
Align external metadata by explicit observation or variable indices, then validate dimensions and uniqueness.
anti_patterns: Do not assume row order matches when adding external metadata to obs or var.
Do not repeatedly subset large backed datasets when one grouped or indexed operation is clearer.
Do not convert sparse matrices to dense arrays unless memory requirements are known and acceptable.

faq.question: What is AnnData used for?
faq.answer: AnnData stores a data matrix with observation metadata, variable metadata, annotations, and analysis results in one structured object.

faq.question: Does this skill only support single-cell genomics?
faq.answer: No. The examples focus on single-cell data, but AnnData can store any annotated matrix with related metadata.

faq.question: Can it help with very large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains backed mode, sparse matrices, chunking, Zarr storage, and categorical metadata for large files.

faq.question: Does it include Scanpy guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how AnnData fits into Scanpy preprocessing, dimensionality reduction, clustering, and visualization workflows.

faq.question: Can it choose the best merge strategy?
faq.answer: It can explain join and merge tradeoffs, but users must confirm the scientific meaning of retained or dropped metadata.

faq.question: Does it download data automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents remote data access patterns, but downloads require an explicit user-approved workflow and trusted source.
